verdicts.strongest_argument: The claim is that a 22% decline is unpriced information, and a decline is the act of pricing. Its sole evidence is quote.json and the baseline already carries it as run_up_20d_pct -20.18 and pct_from_52w_high -30.92, so whatever the persistent seller knew has been transmitted into the level at which this print is struck. The inference layered on top - that even distribution across fifteen sessions implies an informed seller rather than a known catalyst - is unsupported by any dated source and is exactly the run-up-as-evidence argument I am here to stop: it can be told with either sign, since the same bars support 'informed seller' and 'de-risked entry'. The corroboration offered is one Stocktwits post predicting another dollar down, which is a retail opinion about the same chart, not independent evidence. Nothing in filings.json after 2026-08-14 identifies a seller, and no 13D/G amendment or Form 144 in the window is cited, so there is not even a candidate mechanism, only the pattern of the bars.
verdicts.baseline_evidence: Baseline tape: spot 10.01, run_up_5d -3.38%, run_up_20d -20.18%, pct_from_52w_high -30.92%, avg_volume_20d 56,815. The move the finding describes is the baseline's own run-up field. The absence of a volume spike, which the finding treats as its strongest tell, is equally consistent with ordinary drift in a 57k-share-a-day microcap and cuts no direction.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A named seller with a dated filing - a 13D/A reduction, a 144, an S-3 takedown - whose size against the 57k daily volume explains the slide and implies more to come.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is the honest one of the three and it lands in the reachable-but-unconnected band rather than the refuted one. The four accessions are in filings.json - the 8-K with items 5.02/7.01/9.01 accepted 2026-08-06T21:03:54Z, the new-filer Form 3 and Form 4, and the SCHEDULE 13D/A accepted 2026-08-10T22:50:37Z - so the sequence was fully reachable to anyone reading EDGAR three to four weeks before the print, which is why I cannot score it low. But no snapshot in this capture draws the sequence together, names the filer, or sizes the stake, and the 13D/A body is not stored, so the 'activist board settlement' characterisation is the hunter's inference from item codes rather than something the corpus states. The Engine Capital corroboration is a December-2025 document naming a $8m holder, which is a fact about last year's 13F and does not establish who filed in August 2026. Two things cap this below 40 in the other direction as well. The mechanism does not obviously reach the print: a cooperation agreement signed in early August changes the board, not the July-quarter numbers, and the finding itself frames the consequence as 'a floor for a bad print', which is a statement about the reaction's shape, not its direction. And the argument that the market cannot have priced it because the stock fell 22% afterwards is the same circular use of the tape as finding #0 - a $130m issuer can absorb a governance filing and still de-rate on demand.

prior_publication.what_it_says: A 13D amendment was accepted on EDGAR four days after the director-appointment 8-K, publicly available and machine-readable, though its contents are not stored in this capture.
8-K items 5.02/7.01/9.01 announcing the addition of an independent director to the compensation and governance committees.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: quote.json shows no volume signature on 08-06 through 08-11 that would mark the market reacting to the filings, so the price bars neither confirm nor refute pricing; volumes stay in the 25k-67k band the finding itself describes. That is consistent with reachable-but-unnoticed and is the main reason this is 32 rather than 15.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: The 13D/A body showing a cooperation agreement with a strategic-review or sale mandate, which would give the September print a mechanism rather than a coincidence of timing.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This restates published guidance, which the scale puts at the top of the range. The FY27 guide - $200-210m net sales, 5-10% growth, adjusted EBITDA up over 40% - and the Q4 FY26 result it sat on top of are both in the capture as a stored body surfaced in a snapshot (docs/994d48dabaeeaa94ab9820db27a79d7711cb5465.txt, snapshots/20260830T084152Z.json item 1), dated 2026-06-25, and the prior-year Q1 collapse to $29.7m from $41.6m and its -18% reaction are in the baseline's own history (2025-09-04, -18.12%) and in the corpus's Stocktwits timestamps. The hunter concedes the guide is wire copy and claims novelty for 'the arithmetic tension' between a +5-10% annual guide and a quarter that shrank 24%. But that arithmetic is performed by subtracting two numbers that were published in the same press release on the same day, and the market had ten weeks and a 17% up-reaction on 2026-06-26 to do it. The supporting claim that nobody has done it rests again on n_queries=0 across six sweeps, which measures the capture, not the market. The FY26 guidance-withdrawal precedent is likewise from the June-2025 release and is a year-old published fact; age is not novelty.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Carries the Q4 FY26 sales of $47.06m down 24.03% YoY and the FY27 guidance of $200-210m with adjusted EBITDA up over 40%.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The 2026-06-25/26 print is in the baseline history at +17.05%, so the market repriced upward on the release that contained both the weak quarter and the guide - it saw the tension and paid for the guide anyway. The seasonal precedent the finding leans on, 2025-09-04 at -18.12%, is also in the baseline history and is therefore inside the expected_move_pct of 15.09 the print is already struck against.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A dated post-June datapoint on the guided year - a channel check, a retailer order cut, a tariff schedule change - that makes the FY27 range unreachable for a reason not present in the 06-25 release.

interactions: #0 and #2 both use the 22% decline, but for opposite purposes: #2 needs the market to have missed the guidance tension, while #0 needs the market to have been selling hard on something for three weeks. #1 explicitly uses the same decline as evidence that the board settlement was NOT priced, so all three findings are drawing contradictory conclusions from the same set of bars. The Engine Capital document (docs/994d48...) is also doing double duty - it is the guidance source for #2 and the activist corroboration for #1.
corpus_limits: AOUT carries no news items, so there is no sell-side preview, no consensus estimate and no wire coverage in this capture; I cannot test whether the FY27 guide had been re-cut or reaffirmed since 06-25, and its absence is a capture artefact. The 13D/A body is not stored, so the identity and intent of the filer are unverifiable here. The baseline's event_plausibility is 'unknown' with cadence_implausible set, but that is an artefact of the same print being matched twice under amc/bmo/intraday tags; a July-quarter print in early September fits an April fiscal year end, so I treated the event as real.
